items.title: When to Keep PNG
items.description: Scenarios where PNG is still the better choice.
items.content: Keep PNG if: 1) Need universal compatibility (emails, older systems), 2) Working with design tools that don't support WebP, 3) Require lossless quality and file is already small (<50KB), 4) Targeting Safari <14 or IE users. WebP excels for modern web applications with 95%+ browser support.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about PNG to WebP conversion

items.question: Does WebP support transparency like PNG?
items.answer: Yes, WebP fully supports alpha channel transparency with both lossless and lossy modes. WebP's transparency compression is actually more efficient than PNG, especially for images with gradual alpha transitions like soft shadows and glows. You can achieve 30-50% smaller file sizes while maintaining the same transparency quality.

items.question: Which browsers support WebP format?
items.answer: WebP has 95%+ browser support as of 2024. It's supported by Chrome (since 2010), Firefox (since 2019), Edge (since 2018), Safari (since 14.0/2020), and Opera. For older browsers, implement the <picture> element with PNG fallback. Mobile support is excellent - iOS 14+, Android 4.0+ (Chrome), and all modern mobile browsers.

items.question: How much smaller are WebP files compared to PNG?
items.answer: WebP provides 25-35% better compression than PNG in lossless mode with identical quality. In lossy mode, WebP can be 60-80% smaller than PNG while maintaining good visual quality. The exact savings depend on image content - graphics with transparency typically see 30-40% reduction, while complex images can achieve even higher compression ratios.

items.question: Should I use lossless or lossy WebP for PNG conversion?
items.answer: Use lossless WebP for logos, UI elements, screenshots, and graphics requiring perfect quality (25-35% smaller than PNG). Use lossy WebP (quality 85-90) for photos, decorative graphics, and content images where minor quality loss is acceptable (60-80% smaller). Test both modes to find the best balance between file size and quality for your use case.

items.question: Can I convert WebP back to PNG without quality loss?
items.answer: If the original WebP was created in lossless mode, converting back to PNG will result in identical quality. However, if the WebP was created in lossy mode, the quality loss is permanent and cannot be recovered. Always keep original PNG files if you might need to convert back or make future edits.

items.answer: Yes, our PNG to WebP converter is completely free with no registration or payment required. All conversion happens locally in your browser using WebAssembly - your images never leave your device. This ensures 100% privacy and security, with no server uploads or data collection.
